comments.body:
interesting... i can only guess that somehow your browser is not proxying the frontend requests correctly but i'm not sure what the cause is and i can't reproduce it locally either.

the dev setup is basically that we have the mlflow server running at localhost:5000, and the react dev server running at localhost:3000.

via this file, the dev server is supposed to proxy all API requests to the actual mlflow server:

https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/master/mlflow/server/js/src/setupProxy.js#L10

however it looks like something is going wrong in that step for you. the `403 forbidden` response makes me think that something is up with your network set up but i can't be sure. sorry i can't be more helpful here, it's difficult to debug this without being able to repro 🙁

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: In case anyone else stumbles upon this, the problem for me causing 403 errors on macOS was that `localhost:5000` was being used by ControlCenter (as described [here](https://nono.ma/port-5000-used-by-control-center-in-macos-controlce)). Manually editing  `setupProxy.js` to use `5001` instead of `5000` and doing `mlflow ui -p 5001` worked for me.
